truths.truth: The header rule catches the Authorization and Cookie shapes in the spellings they actually take in transcript text, not only the unquoted one the fixture plants
truths.evidence: crates/verbatim-core/src/observe/egress.rs:363-366 skips any header name whose preceding byte is a double quote, deferring to rule 5; rule 5 (redact_json_pairs, :452) only fires on "name": "value", so a header opened by a quote is caught by nothing. Confirmed against the real source compiled standalone: 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-LEAK-1" https://api.example.com' comes back BYTE-IDENTICAL, sentinel intact; likewise 'curl -H "Cookie: sid-LEAK-4"' and 'set Cookie: "sid-LEAK-3"'. The single-quoted spelling is redacted correctly, so this is specific to the double quote. Frequency measured on the same corpus CONTEXT's D-03 used (~/.claude/projects, all 4617 jsonl): 1333 occurrences of 'Authorization:', of which 347 are immediately preceded by a double quote in the message text; Cookie: 5 of ~150.

gaps.name: A double-quoted header shape is redacted by nothing
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - redact_header_spans defers every name whose preceding byte is '"' to the JSON-pair rule (egress.rs:363-366), but the JSON-pair rule only matches "name": "value". A header that opens inside a double-quoted string - the ordinary curl spelling - therefore falls through both rules and ships whole.
gaps.evidence: crates/verbatim-core/src/observe/egress.rs:363-366 (the quote exemption) and :452-490 (redact_json_pairs, which requires a closing quote followed by ':'). Compiled the real egress.rs standalone and ran the rule set: 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-LEAK-1" https://api.example.com' returns byte-identical with the sentinel intact; 'curl -H "Cookie: sid-LEAK-4" -X GET' likewise; 'set Cookie: "sid-LEAK-3" and the rest' likewise. The single-quoted form 'curl -H '\''Authorization: Bearer sk-LEAK-2'\''' IS redacted, which isolates the cause to the double quote. Corpus frequency over ~/.claude/projects (4617 jsonl): 347 of 1333 'Authorization:' occurrences sit immediately behind a double quote, and 5 of ~150 'Cookie:' ones. tests/fixtures/session-secrets.jsonl plants only the unquoted spelling, so no test covers this.
gaps.missing: Let the header rule take a name preceded by a double quote when what follows is not a JSON pair - e.g. only defer to rule 5 when the quoted run actually closes before the colon (bytes[name_start-1] == '"' AND the colon sits outside that quoted string). Then plant 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <sentinel>"' and '-H "Cookie: <sentinel>"' in session-secrets.jsonl so the wire test covers the spelling, and re-state the direction in the module docs, since this is an UNDER-match and the docs currently claim over-matching is the failure direction.
